authors: Pandey, Anil K.; Naduthambi, Devan; Thomas, Krista M.; Zondlo, Neal J.
citation: Journal of the American Chemical Society (2013), 135(11), 4333-4363
reference: Proline Editing: A General and Practical Approach to the Synthesis of Functionally and Structurally Diverse Peptides. Analysis of Steric versus Stereoelectronic Effects of 4-Substituted Prolines on Conformation within Peptides | Pandey, Anil K.; Naduthambi, Devan; Thomas, Krista M.; Zondlo, Neal J. | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2013), 135(11), 4333-4363
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Resin-bound peptide 21' in a fritted tube was swelled in anhydrous DMF (1.0 mL) and anhydrous THF (1.0 mL). Copper iodide (CuI) (19.0 mg, 0.1 mmol) and DIPEA (174 μL, 1.0 mmol) were added, followed by 1-octyne (149 μL, 1.0 mmol). The reaction mixture was allowed to react with gentle mixing at room temperature for 8 h. General procedure A. Cleavage, deprotection, and purification of peptides The peptides on solid phase were washed with DMF (3x) and CH2Cl2 (3x) on a water aspirator. The cleavage of peptides from resin was conducted using 96% TFA, 2% water, and 2% triisopropylsilane (TIS) or triethylsilane (TES) for 30-60 minutes. The solutions were concentrated by evaporation under nitrogen and the peptides were precipitated with cold ether. The precipitate was dissolved in water, filtered, and purified via reverse phase HPLC (Vydac semipreparative C18, 10 x 250 mm, 5 μm particle size, 300 Å pore) using 20 min isocratic 100% buffer A (98% H2O, 2% MeCN, 0.06% TFA), followed by a linear gradient of 0-50% buffer B (80% MeCN, 20% H2O, 0.05% TFA) in buffer A over 60 minutes, unless otherwise indicated. Peptides were purified to homogeneity, as indicated by the presence of a single peak on reinjection on analytical HPLC (Microsorb MV C18, 4.6 x 250 mm, 3-5 μm particle size, 100 Å pore). Peptide 111. Expected mass 685.3, observed mass (M + Na) 708.3, tR = 54.8 min.
notes: solid-supported reaction, Rink-amide resin used

reference: Probe incorporation mediated by enzymes (PRIME) method using lipoic acid ligases and lipoic acid analogs for labeling proteins | Ting, Alice Y.; Liu, Daniel Shao-Chen | World Intellectual Property Organization, WO2013148189 A1 2013-10-03
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Coumarin-triazole standards for azide 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7 (FIG. 4B) were generated from reacting 120 μM of each azide with 100 μM 7-ethynyl coumarin until 7-ethynyl coumarin was fully converted to the triazole adduct, using 100 μM CuSO4, 400 μM THPTA, and 4 mM sodium ascorbate. Complete conversion of 7-ethynyl coumarin to coumarin-triazole was achieved in 30 min for all azides, and was confirmed by thin-layer chromatography, and by monitoring for saturation of turn-on fluorescence levels of coumarin. Such reaction mixture, now representing coumarin-triazole of a known concentration (100 μM), was then mixed with 7-ethynyl coumarin in defined ratios in the presence of 20-fold molar excess of EDTA relative to CuSO4, (which was carried over from the triazole generation reaction), to generate the calibration curve above.
notes: regioselective, Huisgen cycloaddition, conversion 81%

experimental_procedure: The reaction of 20 with 15 was monitored by GC, using a ten-fold excess of 20. Compounds 20 (0.66 mL, 6.0 mmol) and 15 (0.075 mL, 0.6 mmol) were dissolved in a 2:1 mixture of tert-butanol:H2O (3 mL total). CuSO4 (1.5 mg, 0.006 mmol), sodium ascorbate (60 μL of 1M solution in H2O), and dodecane (0.14 mL, 0.6 mmol) were added to the reaction mixture, which was stirred at 25°C. Aliquots of the mixture were quenched with H2O and extracted with 0.2 mL of ether. The ether extract was diluted with 1 mL of CH2Cl2 and analyzed by GC every thirty minutes for the first two hours, and every hour for the remaining time until 50% conversion. Dodecane was used as an internal standard to quantify the consumption of 15.

Such reaction mixture, now representing coumarin-triazole of a known concentration (100 μM), was then mixed with 7-ethynyl coumarin in defined ratios in the presence of 20-fold molar excess of EDTA relative to CuSO4, (which was carried over from the triazole generation reaction), to generate the calibration curve above.
notes: regioselective, Huisgen cycloaddition, conversion 31%

reference: Probe incorporation mediated by enzymes (PRIME) method using lipoic acid ligases and lipoic acid analogs for labeling proteins | Ting, Alice Y.; Liu, Daniel Shao-Chen | World Intellectual Property Organization, WO2013148189 A1 2013-10-03
experimental_procedure: To prepare the triazole adduct between 7-ethynyl coumarin and 6-azidomethylnicotinic acid (azide 4), 7-ethynyl coumarin (20 mg, 0.067 mmol) and 4 (20 mg, 0.11 mmol) were dissolved in DMSO (4 mL). Sodium ascorbate (0.5M solution in water, 59 μL, 0.029 mmol) and copper(II) sulfate (0.25M solution in water, 30 μL, 0.007 mmol) were then added, and the reaction was stirred for 1 hour. After the solvent was removed in vacuo, The resulting residue was taken up in methanol and loaded directly onto a preparative TLC plate (0.25 mm thickness) and the plate was developed with 95:5 acetonitrile:H2O. The product-containing silica was collected and sonicated in chloroform (30 mL) for 3 minutes and filtered. The filtrate was concentrated to deliver the triazole adduct as a tan solid. 7-ethynyl coumarin-azide triazole adduct 4 1H NMR (400 MHz, DMSO-d6): 8.91 (s, 1H), 8.77 (s, 1H), 8.17 (d, 1H, J=8.0 Hz), 7.86-7.75 (m, 3H), 7.34 (d, 1H, J=8.0 Hz), 6.41 (s, 1H), 5.76 (s, 1H), 5.35 (s, 2H), 2.64 (t, 1H, J=6.2 Hz), 2.50-2.45 (m, 2H), 1.86 (s, 1H). 13C NMR (100 MHz, DMSO-d6): 175.0, 173.7, 172.8, 160.4, 155.4, 153.88, 150.7, 150.6, 145.45, 138.4, 134.6, 125.9, 124.3, 122.1, 121.9, 116.7, 113.0, 112.4, 61.5, 54.9, 48.9, 30.0, 29.5, 21.9. HR-ESI-MS: [M+H]+ m/z 479.1203 calculated, 479.1210 observed.
notes: regioselective, Huisgen cycloaddition

citation: Journal of the American Chemical Society (2013), 135(11), 4333-4363
reference: Proline Editing: A General and Practical Approach to the Synthesis of Functionally and Structurally Diverse Peptides. Analysis of Steric versus Stereoelectronic Effects of 4-Substituted Prolines on Conformation within Peptides | Pandey, Anil K.; Naduthambi, Devan; Thomas, Krista M.; Zondlo, Neal J. | Journal of the American Chemical Society (2013), 135(11), 4333-4363
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Solution phase Huisgen azide-alkyne 1,3-cycloaddition of peptide 21 with phenylacetylene: To peptide 21 (150 μM) dissolved in 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.2) containing 250 mM NaCl (500 μL) was added CuSO4•5H2O (50 μL of 10 mM stock in H2O, 0.5 μmol, 1 mM final concentration), sodium ascorbate (5.0 mg, 25 μmol, 50 mM final concentration), phenanthroline (10 μL of 10 mM stock in DMSO, 100 nmol, 200 μM final concentration), and phenylacetylene (3.0 μL, 27 μmol, 54 mM final concentration) consecutively. The reaction mixture was stirred gently for 60 min at 37 °C to obtain peptide 109. The crude reaction mixture was then filtered (0.45 μm Nylon syringe filter) and extracted with diethyl ether and CH2Cl2 to remove excess reagents. The modified peptide was purified via reverse phase analytical HPLC using 20 min isocratic 100% buffer A, followed by a linear gradient of 0-50% buffer B in buffer A over 60 minutes. Peptide 109. Expected mass 677.3, observed mass (M + Na) 700.2, tR = 52.7 min.
notes: Huisgen coupling, phosphate/NaCl buffered solution, alternative preparation shown

experimental_procedure: Coumarin-triazole standards for azide 1, 2, 5, 6, and 7 (FIG. 4B) were generated from reacting 120 μM of each azide with 100 μM 7-ethynyl coumarin until 7-ethynyl coumarin was fully converted to the triazole adduct, using 100 μM CuSO4, 400 μM THPTA, and 4 mM sodium ascorbate. Complete conversion of 7-ethynyl coumarin to coumarin-triazole was achieved in 30 min for all azides, and was confirmed by thin-layer chromatography, and by monitoring for saturation of turn-on fluorescence levels of coumarin. Such reaction mixture, now representing coumarin-triazole of a known concentration (100 μM), was then mixed with 7-ethynyl coumarin in defined ratios in the presence of 20-fold molar excess of EDTA relative to CuSO4, (which was carried over from the triazole generation reaction), to generate the calibration curve above.
notes: regioselective, Huisgen cycloaddition
